sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Cloud hosting run and check setup
sections.what: Tells the Replit cloud service which tools to install, Python 3.13 and Node 24, and how to run the app. The Run button starts the app through scripts/task.py replit and waits for port 5000, which is exposed on external port 80. A separate check runs the frontend build, lint and tests, then the Python tests. A post-merge script runs after code merges, with a three minute limit.
sections.why: Likely reason: the hosting service reads this file to set up the environment and know how to start and check the project.
sections.watch_out: The app's own dev server uses port 5173 while this file expects port 5000, so the two settings must match what the app actually listens on.

summary: Replit cloud configuration. It installs Python 3.13 and Node 24, defines a Run workflow that starts the app and runs project checks, and maps the app's port 5000 to external port 80.
purpose: Lets the project run on Replit with one press of the Run button.
why: The workflow tasks state what runs on Replit. The reason for the separate project checks is not stated.
how: Replit reads this file when the project opens. The Project workflow runs the Start application and project-checks workflows in parallel. Start application runs the replit task. project-checks runs the frontend build, lint, and tests, then the Python tests.
inputs: The Replit environment and the project files.
outputs: A running app on port 5000 and a validation result for project-checks.
risks: The Start application workflow listens on all network interfaces. The project-checks commands are not the same as the full release gate in scripts/task.py, so Replit can pass while the full check would fail. The post-merge script was not reviewed.
debug: If the app is not reachable, check the port mapping and the Replit domain settings. If dependencies are missing, check the .pythonlibs folder.
